# Original LEZAC.EXE compatibility sound-hook cursor/priority evidence,
# captured in-container via DOSBox /proc/mem sampling of the ACCEPTED sound
# pair. The accepted cursor lives at DS:0x78C0 and the accepted priority at
# DS:0x799E; DS:0x2074 / DS:0x799F are the PENDING scratch pair, which many
# unrelated routines write (an earlier sampling attempt on the pending word
# produced only noise, which is why the accepted pair is authoritative here).
#
# objective_pickup: the player was positioned on the level-1 objective tile
# (tile id 108 at tile 27,15 -> world 216,120) and the game's own pickup
# logic fired; the accepted pair was read at the exact tick the objective
# counter DS:0x2088 went 0 -> 1.
#
# level_complete: the level-1 objective counters were seeded to their targets
# (the technique tools/seed_original_level.py uses: DS:0x2088 <- DS:0x2086,
# DS:0x79B5 <- DS:0x79B3) so the game derived its own completion flags; the
# accepted pair was read as the completion banner opened. This value also
# matches the static banner routine at file 0x250c..0x2517, which writes
# `mov WORD PTR ds:0x2074,0x3d` then `mov BYTE PTR ds:0x799f,0xa`.
#
# The player-damage sound was observed in the same runs starting at cursor
# 0x002d priority 4, independently confirming the port's existing
# kPlayerDamageSoundCursor = 0x002d and that a start value identifies a
# sound (the accepted cursor then advances as the sound plays out).
sound_callsite_original=level1
source=LEZAC.EXE via DOSBox /proc/mem runtime read
runtime_ds=0c8f
accepted_cursor_offset=0x78c0
accepted_priority_offset=0x799e
pending_cursor_offset=0x2074
pending_priority_offset=0x799f
objective_counter_offset=0x2088
hook objective_pickup cursor=0x0000 priority=3 evidence=runtime_counter_transition
hook level_complete cursor=0x003d priority=10 evidence=runtime_and_static_0x250c
corroboration player_damage cursor=0x002d priority=4
visual_claim=0
temp_copy=1
